scenario: 为 10 亿用户从 5 亿候选视频里做推荐，p99 延迟预算只有 200ms。
scenario_en: Recommend for 1B users over 500M candidate videos with a p99 latency budget of only 200ms.
q: 检索+排序的「三级漏斗」按顺序是哪三层？
q_en: What are the three stages of the retrieval-and-ranking funnel, in order?
why: 漏斗每级都是「更强的模型、更少的候选」：候选生成十亿→千级(10-20ms)、粗排千级→百级(10-30ms)、精排百级→最终(20-50ms)。顺序必须由宽到深，重模型只在小集合上跑才付得起。
why_en: The funnel runs candidate generation (billions to thousands), then coarse ranking (thousands to hundreds), then fine re-ranking (hundreds), each stage spending a heavier model on fewer items.
diagram:
flowchart LR A["5亿候选"] --> B["候选生成
两塔ANN · 10-20ms"] B --> C["~1000
粗排 · 10-30ms"] C --> D["~100
精排 · 20-50ms"] D --> E["最终结果"]
options: 候选生成：两塔 ANN 从十亿粗筛到千级 → 粗排：轻量模型给千级打分留~100 → 精排：重模型精排~100
粗排：轻量模型先给十亿全量打分 → 候选生成：ANN 再压到千级 → 精排：重模型出最终结果
精排：重模型直接对全部候选打分 → 候选生成：负责去重降载 → 粗排：最后套业务规则收尾
候选生成：ANN 粗筛 → 精排：重模型直接排序 → 粗排：轻量模型再做一次二次兜底
options_en: Candidate generation: two-tower ANN narrows billions to thousands → coarse ranking: light model scores the thousands down to ~100 → fine re-ranking: heavy model re-ranks the ~100.
Coarse ranking: a light model scores all billions first → candidate generation: ANN then compresses to thousands → fine re-ranking: heavy model produces the final result.
Fine re-ranking: heavy model scores all candidates directly → candidate generation: handles dedup and load shedding → coarse ranking: applies business rules at the end.
Candidate generation: ANN pre-filters → fine re-ranking: heavy model sorts directly → coarse ranking: light model does a second fallback pass.
optionExplanations: 对；由宽到深，候选生成先把量降到千级，粗排再降到百级，精排才用得起最贵的模型。
顺序颠倒：让轻量模型先给十亿全量打分正是三级漏斗要避免的算力灾难，候选生成必须在最前面。
重模型对 5 亿候选逐个打分算不完，正是没有候选生成会崩的那条路径。
精排放粗排前面就白白让重模型处理了更多候选，违背「越往后候选越少、模型越重」的原则。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — broad to deep: candidate generation drops volume to thousands, coarse ranking to hundreds, so fine re-ranking can afford the most expensive model.
Backwards: scoring all billions with any model first is the compute disaster the funnel exists to avoid; candidate generation must come first.
A heavy model cannot score 500M candidates in budget — this is exactly the path that breaks without candidate generation.
Putting fine re-ranking before coarse ranking wastes the heavy model on more items, violating fewer-items-heavier-model ordering.

termDefinitions.meaning: 近似最近邻检索：不保证精确，但能在十亿向量里毫秒级找出最相似的 top-k。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ANN (Approximate Nearest Neighbor) search finds the most similar top-k vectors among billions in milliseconds, trading exactness for speed.

termDefinitions.meaning: 漏斗第一级：用两塔+ANN 把海量物料快速粗筛到几百到几千个候选。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Candidate generation is the funnel's first stage, quickly narrowing a huge corpus to a few hundred to few thousand candidates via two-tower + ANN.

q: 把「为什么要分三级漏斗」的推理链排成正确顺序：
q_en: Order the reasoning for why the pipeline is split into three funnel stages:
steps: 候选集降到千级后，粗排用轻量模型进一步筛到百级
单个模型无法在延迟预算内给 5 亿物料逐个打分
百级小集合上才付得起精排的重模型(DCN/多任务/transformer)
所以先用两塔 ANN 把十亿快速粗筛到千级
why: 推理起点是「一个模型算不完全量」这个约束，于是逐级用更强模型换更少候选：ANN 先降到千级 → 粗排降到百级 → 精排在百级上跑重模型。每一步都是拿广度换深度。
why_en: It starts from the constraint that no single model can score all items in budget, so each stage trades breadth for depth: ANN to thousands, coarse ranking to hundreds, then a heavy model on the hundreds.

termDefinitions.meaning: 精排常用模型：显式建模特征交叉，比 MLP 更能学到高阶交互。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: DCN (Deep Cross Network) explicitly models feature crosses, capturing higher-order interactions better than a plain MLP.

scenario: 面试官问：既然精排模型最准，为什么不直接用它给全部 5 亿候选打分，省掉前两级？
scenario_en: The interviewer asks: since the fine-ranking model is most accurate, why not just score all 500M candidates with it and skip the earlier stages?
q: 为什么要分级而不是用最强模型对全量打分？
q_en: Why stage the pipeline instead of running the strongest model over everything?
why: 精排模型每个候选要几毫秒，5 亿候选根本算不完，且大多数是明显无关项。分级把重模型省到最后的百级小集合上，用广度换深度。
why_en: The fine model costs milliseconds per item, so scoring 500M is impossible in budget and most items are obviously irrelevant; staging saves the heavy model for the final ~100.
tradeoff: 分级(省算力但可能漏召回) vs 全量精排(最准但算不完)
whenOtherWins: 如果候选池本身只有几百个(如小型商品目录),就不需要漏斗,直接用一个精排模型全量打分反而更简单准确。
options: 因为精排模型只支持一次处理几百条输入,是框架的硬性 batch 上限,所以必须先砍到百级
因为候选生成的两塔模型比精排更准,精排只是用来做最后的多样性去重
因为对 5 亿候选逐个跑精排在延迟预算内算不完,且大多数明显无关,重模型该省到最后小集合
因为精排必须在 CPU 上跑而候选生成在 GPU 上,硬件不同所以要拆成两级流水线
options_en: Because the fine model can only take a few hundred inputs at once — a hard framework batch cap — so you must cut to hundreds first.
Because the two-tower model in candidate generation is more accurate than the fine model, which just does final dedup and diversity.
Because running the fine model over 500M candidates cannot finish in budget and most are obviously irrelevant, so the heavy model is saved for the final small set.
Because the fine model must run on CPU while candidate generation runs on GPU, so the hardware split forces two stages.
optionExplanations: batch 上限是可调工程参数,不是分级的根因;真正的原因是全量精排的总算力/延迟付不起。
说反了:两塔为速度牺牲了精度,精排才是最准的一级,不是只做去重。
对;约束是延迟预算 × 候选数,重模型只在广度已被砍小后才跑得起,这就是漏斗的意义。
硬件不是根因,候选生成和精排都能上 GPU;分级是为了控制总算力与延迟。
optionExplanations_en: Batch size is a tunable engineering knob, not the root reason; the real driver is that full fine-scoring cannot afford the compute/latency.
Reversed: the two-tower trades accuracy for speed, and the fine model is the most accurate stage, not just a dedup step.
Correct — the constraint is latency budget × candidate count, so the heavy model only runs once breadth is already cut, which is the funnel's whole point.
Hardware is not the root cause; both stages can run on GPU, and staging exists to control total compute and latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 漏斗最后一级:用最贵最准的模型对~100个候选精细排序,并叠加业务规则。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fine re-ranking is the last stage, applying the most expensive, most accurate model to ~100 candidates plus business overlays.

scenario: 一个相关物料在候选生成阶段没被 ANN 召回,后面粗排和精排都没机会再见到它。
scenario_en: A relevant item is not retrieved by ANN in candidate generation, so coarse and fine ranking never see it.
q: 候选生成的漏项会造成什么后果,为什么它是杠杆最高的一级?
q_en: What is the consequence of a miss in candidate generation, and why is it the highest-leverage stage?
why: 漏斗只会往下删、不会往上加,候选生成漏掉的物料下游永远找不回来,所以它的 recall@k 是天花板。粗排/精排再强也只能在已召回集合里排序。
why_en: The funnel only removes items downstream, so anything missed in candidate generation can never be recovered, making its recall@k the ceiling for the whole system.
options: 漏掉的物料会在精排阶段被重模型自动补回,所以候选生成的召回率影响不大
漏掉的物料下游永远无法恢复,候选生成的 recall@k 是整条链路的天花板,是杠杆最高的一级
漏项只影响延迟不影响质量,因为候选越少后面算得越快、体验反而更好
漏掉的物料会进入一个二级召回队列,下一次请求时再补进来,单次请求不受影响
options_en: A missed item is automatically recovered by the heavy model in fine re-ranking, so candidate-generation recall barely matters.
A missed item can never be recovered downstream, so candidate-generation recall@k caps the whole pipeline — it is the highest-leverage stage.
Misses only affect latency, not quality, since fewer candidates make later stages faster and the experience better.
Missed items go into a secondary retrieval queue and are added on the next request, so a single request is unaffected.
optionExplanations: 错;精排只能对「已召回」的集合排序,它看不见没被召回的物料,补不回来。
对;这就是为什么候选生成盯 recall@k、其余阶段盯精度,漏召回是不可逆损失。
漏项直接损失了本该展示的相关内容,是质量损失而非单纯的延迟优化。
没有这种自动二级队列;漏召回就是当次结果里少了这个相关项,不会自动回补。
optionExplanations_en: Wrong — fine re-ranking only sorts the already-retrieved set; it cannot see items that were never retrieved.
Correct — this is why candidate generation optimizes recall@k while later stages optimize precision; a miss is an irreversible loss.
A miss directly loses relevant content that should have shown, which is a quality loss, not just a latency win.
There is no such automatic secondary queue; a miss simply means that relevant item is absent from this result, with no auto-backfill.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在返回的前 k 个结果里,覆盖了多少真正相关物料的比例;候选生成的核心指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Recall@k is the fraction of truly relevant items captured within the top-k returned, the key metric for candidate generation.

scenario: 候选生成要在 10-20ms 内从十亿物料里找出相关候选,不能对每对 user-item 现算一个大模型。
scenario_en: Candidate generation must find relevant items among billions in 10-20ms, without running a big model on each user-item pair.
q: 两塔(two-tower)模型的结构和「联合训练」为什么能支撑毫秒级检索?
q_en: How does the two-tower model's structure and joint training enable millisecond retrieval?
why: query 塔吃用户上下文、item 塔吃物料特征,输出同维 embedding,联合训练让相关 pair 的向量靠近(余弦相似)。因为两塔独立,item 向量可离线预算入 ANN 索引,线上只算 query 向量再查 ANN。
why_en: The query tower encodes user context and the item tower encodes item features into same-dim embeddings, trained jointly so relevant pairs sit close, letting item vectors be precomputed offline into an ANN index.
diagram:
flowchart LR U["用户上下文"] --> QT["query 塔"] I["物料特征"] --> IT["item 塔"] QT --> QE["query embedding"] IT --> IE["item embedding
(离线预算入ANN)"] QE -. 余弦相似 .- IE
options: query 塔和 item 塔联合训练成同维 embedding,相关 pair 靠近;item 向量离线预算入 ANN,线上只算 query 再查
两塔共享同一套权重,对每个 user-item 对在线拼接后过一个深层网络算出精确分数
query 塔离线预算所有用户向量,item 塔在线为每个候选实时编码,再逐对算点积排序
两塔分别训练、互不影响,靠一个额外的交叉注意力层在线融合 user 和 item 特征
options_en: Query and item towers are trained jointly into same-dim embeddings so relevant pairs sit close; item vectors are precomputed offline into ANN, and only the query is computed online.
Both towers share one set of weights and, for each user-item pair, concatenate online and pass through a deep network to compute an exact score.
The query tower precomputes all user vectors offline while the item tower encodes each candidate online in real time, then dot-products every pair.
The towers are trained separately and independently, fused online by an extra cross-attention layer over user and item features.
optionExplanations: 对;两塔分离是关键——item 侧能离线算好入索引,线上只剩一次 query 编码+ANN 查询,毫秒完成。
在线对每对过深层网络正是两塔要避免的,那是精排的做法,十亿量级算不完。
反了;是 item 向量离线预算、query 在线算,而非相反,且不做逐对点积而是 ANN 近似检索。
两塔必须联合训练才能让 query 和 item 落到同一可比空间;在线交叉注意力破坏了可预算性。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — tower separation is the key: item vectors are precomputed into the index, leaving only one query encode plus an ANN lookup online, done in milliseconds.
Running a deep network per pair online is exactly what two-tower avoids; that is the fine-ranking approach and cannot scale to billions.
Reversed: item vectors are precomputed and the query is computed online, and it uses ANN, not exhaustive per-pair dot products.
The towers must be trained jointly so query and item land in one comparable space; online cross-attention breaks precomputability.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两个独立编码器分别把 user 和 item 映射成同维向量,用向量相似度做匹配。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A two-tower model uses two separate encoders to map user and item into same-dim vectors, matched by vector similarity.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把对象压成一个稠密向量,语义相近的对象向量距离近。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An embedding is a dense vector representation where semantically similar objects have nearby vectors.

scenario: 候选生成阶段要在十亿级物料上给出可供后续排序的候选集。
scenario_en: The candidate-generation stage must return a workable candidate set from billions of items.
q: 候选生成大致把量级从多少降到多少、用多长时间?这个规模决定了什么?
q_en: Roughly what count and latency does candidate generation target, and what does that size decide?
why: 经验量级:十亿物料 → ~500-2000 候选,10-20ms 内完成。这个「千级」输出规模是粗排的输入基数,决定后面 feature store 要批量取多少行特征、粗排要给多少候选打分。
why_en: Rough anchor: billions to ~500-2000 candidates in 10-20ms, and this thousands-scale output sets the base load for coarse ranking's feature fetches and scoring.
options: 从十亿降到~10 个候选,耗时约 100-200ms,直接就是最终展示给用户的结果集
从十亿降到~500-2000 个候选,10-20ms 完成,这个千级规模是粗排的输入基数
从十亿降到~100 万候选,约 1s 完成,再交给精排逐个用重模型打分
从十亿降到固定 256 个候选,耗时约 50ms,数量固定是为了对齐 GPU batch
options_en: From billions to ~10 candidates in about 100-200ms, which is directly the final set shown to the user.
From billions to ~500-2000 candidates in 10-20ms, and this thousands-scale count is the input base for coarse ranking.
From billions to ~1M candidates in about 1s, then handed to fine re-ranking to score each with the heavy model.
From billions to a fixed 256 candidates in about 50ms, fixed to align with the GPU batch size.
optionExplanations: ~10 是最终结果的量级,不是候选生成的输出;还要经过粗排精排两级才轮到它变这么小。
对;千级候选 + 10-20ms 是标准锚点,它决定了粗排要处理多少候选、取多少特征。
百万候选精排根本算不完;候选生成的意义正是把量降到千级而非百万。
候选数不是为对齐 batch 固定死的,而是由 recall 需求和下游预算决定的动态量级。
optionExplanations_en: ~10 is the final result scale, not candidate generation's output; it only shrinks that far after coarse and fine ranking.
Correct — thousands of candidates in 10-20ms is the standard anchor, and it sets how many candidates coarse ranking scores and how many features it fetches.
Fine re-ranking cannot score a million candidates; candidate generation exists precisely to cut to thousands, not millions.
Candidate count is not fixed to match a batch; it is a dynamic scale set by recall needs and downstream budget.

termDefinitions.meaning: 检索返回相似度最高的 k 个结果;这里 k 约为几百到几千。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Top-k returns the k most similar results; here k is roughly a few hundred to a few thousand.

scenario: 两塔上线时,item 有十亿个而 query(用户上下文)每次请求都不同。要在 10ms 内查到候选。
scenario_en: At serving time there are billions of items while the query (user context) differs each request, and candidates must return in 10ms.
q: 两塔的哪一侧该离线预算、哪一侧在线算?为什么这样切?
q_en: Which tower is precomputed offline vs computed online, and why split it this way?
why: item 向量离线批量算好、灌进 ANN 索引;线上只对当次 query 算一个向量,再查 ANN 取 top-k。因为 item 集合巨大但相对稳定,query 小但每次都变——把不变的大集合预算掉,只在线算多变的小部分。
why_en: Item vectors are precomputed into the ANN index while only the per-request query vector is computed online, because items are huge but stable and the query is small but always changing.
tradeoff: item 离线预算(省在线算力但索引会漂移) vs 全在线(永远最新但十亿量级算不动)
whenOtherWins: 如果 item 特征高频变化(如实时价格、库存),离线预算的 embedding 会很快过期,这时需要流式重算 item 向量或把易变特征挪到粗排阶段处理。
options: query 向量离线预算好所有用户,item 向量在线为每个候选实时编码后逐对比对
两侧都在线算:每次请求同时编码 query 和全部 item 向量,保证绝对新鲜
item 向量离线批量算入 ANN 索引,线上只算当次 query 向量再查 ANN 取 top-k
两侧都离线预算:把所有 user×item 的相似度提前算成一张大表,线上直接查表
options_en: Query vectors are precomputed for all users offline, while item vectors are encoded online per candidate and compared pairwise.
Compute both online: encode the query and all item vectors on every request to guarantee absolute freshness.
Item vectors are precomputed offline into the ANN index; online you only compute the current query vector and look up top-k in ANN.
Precompute both offline: materialize the full user×item similarity table ahead of time and just read it online.
optionExplanations: 反了;用户上下文每次请求都变、无法预算全,能预算的是相对稳定的 item 侧。
在线编码十亿 item 每次请求都算不完,正是两塔要绕开的算力灾难。
对;把不变的大集合(item)离线灌进索引,只在线算多变的小部分(query),毫秒级完成。
user×item 全量相似度表是十亿×十亿量级,存不下也没法及时更新,不可行。
optionExplanations_en: Reversed — user context changes every request and cannot be fully precomputed; the stable item side is what gets precomputed.
Encoding a billion items online per request cannot finish; this is the compute disaster two-tower avoids.
Correct — precompute the large stable set (items) into the index and compute only the small changing part (query) online, done in milliseconds.
A full user×item similarity table is billions×billions in size — unstorable and impossible to keep fresh.

termDefinitions.meaning: 预先组织好的向量索引结构,支持毫秒级查最相似的 top-k。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An ANN index is a pre-built vector structure that answers top-k nearest-neighbor queries in milliseconds.

scenario: 训练两塔时,只有「用户点过的正样本」,没有天然的负样本告诉模型哪些 item 不相关。
scenario_en: Training the two towers, you only have positive samples (items the user engaged) and no natural negatives telling the model which items are irrelevant.
q: 两塔训练怎么造负样本?in-batch negatives 和 hard-negative mining 各解决什么?
q_en: How does two-tower training source negatives, and what do in-batch negatives vs hard-negative mining each solve?
why: in-batch negatives:把同一 batch 里别人的正 item 当作当前 query 的负样本,几乎零成本造大量负例。但这些多是「太容易」的负例,再加 hard-negative mining——挑那些相似但实际不相关的难负例——逼模型学会细分边界。
why_en: In-batch negatives reuse other queries' positive items in the batch as negatives almost for free, while hard-negative mining adds similar-but-irrelevant items to force sharper decision boundaries.
options: 两塔不需要负样本,只用正样本做回归,让相关 pair 的相似度回归到 1 即可
把整个物料库随机采样当负例,采样越多越好,不需要区分难易
in-batch negatives 复用同 batch 其他正 item 当负例(近乎免费),hard-negative mining 再补相似难负例练边界
只用人工标注的负样本,标注者逐条标出哪些 item 与 query 不相关
options_en: Two towers need no negatives; train on positives only, regressing relevant pairs' similarity toward 1.
Randomly sample the entire corpus as negatives, the more the better, with no need to distinguish easy from hard.
In-batch negatives reuse other positives in the batch as negatives (nearly free); hard-negative mining then adds similar hard negatives to sharpen boundaries.
Use only human-labeled negatives, with annotators marking item by item which are irrelevant to the query.
optionExplanations: 没有负例模型学不到「什么不相关」,只压正 pair 会让所有向量塌到一起。
纯随机负例大多太容易(明显不相关),模型学不到相似项之间的细分边界。
对;in-batch 近乎免费但偏易,hard negatives 专挑相似难例,两者互补。
逐条人工标负样本成本极高、无法覆盖十亿量级,工业界靠 in-batch + hard mining。
optionExplanations_en: Without negatives the model cannot learn what is irrelevant; pushing only positives collapses all vectors together.
Purely random negatives are mostly too easy (obviously irrelevant), so the model never learns fine boundaries between similar items.
Correct — in-batch negatives are nearly free but easy, and hard-negative mining targets similar hard cases; the two complement each other.
Hand-labeling negatives item by item is prohibitively costly and cannot cover billions; industry uses in-batch plus hard mining.

termDefinitions.meaning: 训练时把同一 batch 里其他样本的正 item 当作当前 query 的负例,免额外采样。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: In-batch negatives treat other samples' positive items within the same batch as negatives for the current query, avoiding extra sampling.

termDefinitions.term: hard-negative mining / 难负样本挖掘
termDefinitions.meaning: 刻意挑选与 query 相似但实际不相关的样本作负例,逼模型学细分边界。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hard-negative mining deliberately picks items similar to the query but actually irrelevant, forcing the model to learn finer boundaries.

scenario: item embedding 已离线灌入 ANN 索引,但物料的属性/热度在变,索引却没有及时重建。
scenario_en: Item embeddings were loaded offline into the ANN index, but item attributes/popularity change while the index is not refreshed in time.
q: embedding drift(嵌入漂移)是什么、怎么发生、如何缓解?
q_en: What is embedding drift, how does it happen, and how do you mitigate it?
why: 正常:离线算好的 item 向量代表当前物料语义。异常:物料变了但索引没重建→旧向量与真实语义脱节→检索悄悄退化、recall 下降却无报错。缓解:周期性重建索引或流式增量更新。代价:重建耗资源、流式更新增加系统复杂度。
why_en: Embedding drift is when item attributes change but the index is not rebuilt, so stale vectors silently degrade retrieval and lower recall with no error; mitigate with periodic re-indexing or streaming updates.
diagram:
flowchart LR A["item 属性变化"] --> B["索引未重建"] B --> C["旧向量脱离真实语义"] C --> D["recall 悄悄下降
无报错"] D -->|缓解| E["周期重建 / 流式更新"] E --> B
options: embedding drift 指 GPU 显存里向量被随机翻转的硬件位错误,靠 ECC 内存纠正
旧 item 向量与物料真实语义脱节→检索悄悄退化 recall 下降;缓解靠周期重建索引或流式增量更新
指训练时 loss 不收敛导致 embedding 发散,靠调小学习率解决,与线上索引无关
指用户 query 分布随时间变化,只需重训 query 塔即可,item 索引无需动
options_en: Embedding drift is a hardware bit-flip of vectors in GPU memory, corrected by ECC RAM.
Stale item vectors detach from items' true meaning → retrieval silently degrades and recall drops; mitigate with periodic re-indexing or streaming updates.
It means training loss diverges so embeddings blow up, fixed by lowering the learning rate, unrelated to the serving index.
It means the user query distribution shifts over time, needing only a query-tower retrain, with no change to the item index.
optionExplanations: 这是硬件位翻转,不是 embedding drift;drift 是语义层面的过期,不是内存错误。
对;危险在于「无报错的悄悄退化」——recall 掉了但系统不报错,得靠重建/流式更新止损。
训练发散是另一回事;drift 说的是线上索引里的向量随物料变化而过期。
query 分布漂移是另一种问题;此处 drift 特指 item 索引里的向量过期,需重建 item 索引。
optionExplanations_en: That is a hardware bit-flip, not embedding drift; drift is semantic staleness, not a memory error.
Correct — the danger is silent degradation with no error: recall falls quietly, so periodic re-indexing or streaming updates are needed to stem it.
Training divergence is a different issue; drift is about serving-index vectors going stale as items change.
Query-distribution shift is a separate problem; this drift is specifically stale item vectors in the index, needing an item-index rebuild.

termDefinitions.meaning: 索引里的物料向量因物料变化而过期,与真实语义脱节,导致检索质量悄悄下降。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Embedding drift is when indexed item vectors go stale as items change, detaching from true meaning and quietly degrading retrieval.

scenario: 要为十亿向量选 ANN 索引结构,理解 HNSW、IVF、PQ 各自的机制与代价。
scenario_en: Choosing an ANN index structure for a billion vectors, you compare the mechanisms and costs of HNSW, IVF, and PQ.
q: HNSW、IVF、PQ 三种 ANN 结构分别靠什么机制、各自的主要代价是什么?
q_en: What mechanism does each of HNSW, IVF, and PQ use, and what is each one's main cost?
why: HNSW=多层可导航图,高层长程边快速跳转、低层细化精度,recall 高但内存/构建贵。IVF=k-means 把空间切成 Voronoi 单元,只搜最近 nprobe 个单元,nprobe 越大 recall 越高、延迟线性上升。PQ=把向量切段各自量化到码本质心,压缩 10-50× 但损一点精度,常与 IVF 组合成 IVF+PQ。
why_en: HNSW is a multi-layer navigable graph (high recall but memory/build-heavy), IVF partitions space into Voronoi cells searched by nprobe (higher nprobe trades latency for recall), and PQ quantizes sub-vectors to codebook centroids for 10-50x compression at some accuracy cost.
tradeoff: HNSW(高 recall,吃内存) vs IVF(nprobe 调 recall/延迟) vs PQ(省内存,损精度)
options: HNSW=多层可导航图(高 recall 但吃内存),IVF=Voronoi 单元搜 nprobe(调 recall/延迟),PQ=子向量量化压缩 10-50×损点精度
三者都是精确检索,区别只是编程语言:HNSW 用 C++、IVF 用 Python、PQ 用 CUDA
HNSW 靠磁盘顺序扫描、IVF 靠哈希分桶、PQ 靠 B+ 树索引,三者互斥不可组合
HNSW 压缩内存最狠、IVF 精度最高无损、PQ 是唯一多层图结构,常单独使用
options_en: HNSW = multi-layer navigable graph (high recall but memory-heavy), IVF = Voronoi cells searched by nprobe (tunes recall/latency), PQ = sub-vector quantization compressing 10-50x at slight accuracy cost.
All three are exact search, differing only in language: HNSW in C++, IVF in Python, PQ in CUDA.
HNSW scans disk sequentially, IVF hashes into buckets, PQ uses a B+ tree, and the three are mutually exclusive and cannot combine.
HNSW compresses memory the most, IVF is highest-precision and lossless, and PQ is the only multi-layer graph, usually used alone.
optionExplanations: 对;三者机制清晰:图导航(HNSW)、单元剪枝(IVF)、码本压缩(PQ),常 IVF+PQ 组合。
它们都是「近似」检索不是精确,区别在结构不在语言。
机制描述全错;且 IVF+PQ 恰恰是常见组合,并非互斥。
反了:PQ 才是压缩最狠的,HNSW 是多层图,IVF 有损;PQ 常与 IVF 组合而非单用。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — clear mechanisms: graph navigation (HNSW), cell pruning (IVF), codebook compression (PQ), often combined as IVF+PQ.
All three are approximate, not exact, and differ by structure, not programming language.
The mechanisms are all wrong, and IVF+PQ is in fact a common combination, not mutually exclusive.
Reversed: PQ compresses the most, HNSW is the multi-layer graph, IVF is lossy, and PQ usually combines with IVF rather than standing alone.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多层图索引:高层稀疏长程边快速定位,低层稠密边精细搜索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HNSW (Hierarchical Navigable Small World) is a multi-layer graph index: sparse long-range links up top for fast jumps, dense links below for fine search.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用 k-means 把向量空间切成 Voronoi 单元,查询只搜最近的 nprobe 个单元。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IVF (Inverted File) partitions the vector space into Voronoi cells via k-means and searches only the nearest nprobe cells.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把向量切成子段,每段量化到学到的码本质心,大幅压缩内存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: PQ (Product Quantization) splits a vector into sub-segments and quantizes each to a learned codebook centroid, heavily compressing memory.

termDefinitions.meaning: 以聚类中心划分的空间区域,每个点归属最近的中心。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Voronoi cell is a region of space around a cluster center, with each point assigned to its nearest center.

scenario: 十亿 FP32 向量若全量驻内存,成本高得离谱,需要压缩才能放进 ANN 索引。
scenario_en: A billion FP32 vectors held fully in memory is prohibitively costly, so compression is needed to fit them in the ANN index.
q: PQ(Product Quantization)大致能压缩多少倍内存?代价是什么、下游影响什么?
q_en: Roughly how much memory does PQ compress, at what cost, and what does it affect downstream?
why: PQ 把向量切段、每段用码本质心的 id 代替原始浮点,大致压缩 10-50×。代价是量化误差→recall 略降。它决定十亿向量能否放进内存索引,直接影响单机能存多少物料、要不要分片。
why_en: PQ replaces each sub-vector with a codebook-centroid id, compressing memory roughly 10-50x at the cost of some recall loss, deciding whether a billion vectors fit in an in-memory index.
options: 压缩约 2×,代价是延迟翻倍,决定要不要上 GPU
压缩约 10-50×,代价是量化误差使 recall 略降,决定十亿向量能否驻内存、要不要分片
压缩约 1000×,几乎无损,所以可以永远单机放下任意规模,不用分片
不压缩内存,只压缩磁盘 IO,代价是构建时间变长,decode 时才解压
options_en: About 2x compression, at the cost of doubled latency, deciding whether to move to GPU.
About 10-50x compression, at the cost of quantization error slightly lowering recall, deciding whether a billion vectors fit in memory and whether to shard.
About 1000x compression, essentially lossless, so any scale always fits on one machine with no sharding.
It compresses disk IO, not memory, at the cost of longer build time, decompressing only at decode.
optionExplanations: 2× 远低于 PQ 的实际压缩比;PQ 靠码本量化能到 10-50×。
对;10-50× 是标准锚点,拿 recall 换内存,直接决定内存索引容量与是否分片。
1000× 且无损不现实;PQ 是有损量化,压缩比也在 10-50× 量级。
PQ 压的就是向量内存占用(码本 id 代替浮点),不是只压磁盘 IO。
optionExplanations_en: 2x is far below PQ's real ratio; codebook quantization reaches 10-50x.
Correct — 10-50x is the standard anchor, trading recall for memory, directly setting in-memory index capacity and whether to shard.
1000x and lossless is unrealistic; PQ is lossy quantization with a 10-50x-scale ratio.
PQ compresses vector memory footprint (codebook ids replacing floats), not just disk IO.

termDefinitions.meaning: PQ 为每个子段学到的一组质心;向量子段用最近质心的 id 表示。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A codebook is the set of centroids PQ learns per sub-segment; each sub-vector is stored as the id of its nearest centroid.

scenario: 用 IVF 索引,发现召回率偏低漏掉相关项,想调 nprobe 参数来救。
scenario_en: Using an IVF index, recall is low and misses relevant items, so you consider tuning nprobe.
q: 调大 IVF 的 nprobe 会怎样?这个取舍的代价在哪?
q_en: What happens when you raise IVF's nprobe, and where is the tradeoff?
why: nprobe = 查询时搜索多少个最近的 Voronoi 单元。调大→覆盖更多候选单元→recall 上升,但要扫的单元变多→延迟近似线性上升。所以 nprobe 是 IVF 上「召回 vs 延迟」的直接旋钮。
why_en: nprobe is how many nearest Voronoi cells a query searches; raising it covers more candidates and lifts recall but scans more cells, so latency rises roughly linearly.
tradeoff: nprobe 大(recall 高、延迟高) vs nprobe 小(延迟低、易漏召回)
options: nprobe 越大 recall 越高、延迟近似线性上升;它是 IVF 上召回 vs 延迟的直接旋钮
nprobe 只影响构建时间,查询延迟不受影响,所以尽量设到最大总没错
nprobe 越大延迟越低、recall 越低,和直觉相反,是用精度换速度的开关
nprobe 控制 PQ 的压缩率,与召回无关,主要影响索引占用的内存大小
options_en: Higher nprobe raises recall with roughly linear latency increase; it is IVF's direct recall-vs-latency knob.
nprobe only affects build time, not query latency, so setting it as high as possible is always safe.
Higher nprobe lowers latency and lowers recall — counterintuitively a precision-for-speed switch.
nprobe controls PQ's compression ratio, unrelated to recall, mainly affecting index memory footprint.
optionExplanations: 对;多搜单元多找回相关项(recall↑)但扫描量增加(延迟↑),典型召回-延迟权衡。
nprobe 直接决定查询要扫多少单元,是查询期开销,不是构建期;设满会顶破延迟预算。
方向说反了:nprobe 大是 recall 高、延迟高,不是延迟低。
nprobe 是 IVF 的搜索广度参数,与 PQ 压缩率是两回事。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — more cells find more relevant items (recall up) but scan more (latency up), the classic recall-latency tradeoff.
nprobe directly sets how many cells a query scans — a query-time cost, not build-time; maxing it blows the latency budget.
Direction is reversed: high nprobe means high recall and high latency, not low latency.
nprobe is IVF's search-breadth parameter, separate from PQ's compression ratio.

termDefinitions.meaning: IVF 查询时搜索的最近 Voronoi 单元数量,越大覆盖越广、越慢。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: nprobe is the number of nearest Voronoi cells an IVF query searches; larger means broader coverage and slower queries.

scenario: 自建 HNSW 索引,要调 ef_construction 和 M 两个关键参数来平衡质量与资源。
scenario_en: Self-hosting an HNSW index, you tune the two key parameters ef_construction and M to balance quality against resources.
q: HNSW 的 ef_construction 和 M 分别控制什么?调大有什么代价?
q_en: What do HNSW's ef_construction and M each control, and what is the cost of raising them?
why: M = 每个节点的连边数(图的稠密度);ef_construction = 建图时每步考察的候选数(建图质量)。两者调大→recall 更高,但代价是更多内存(M)和更长构建时间(ef_construction)。能报出这两个参数说明有 ANN 实操经验。
why_en: M is the number of links per node (graph density) and ef_construction is the build-time candidate breadth; raising either improves recall at the cost of more memory (M) and longer build time (ef_construction).
options: ef_construction 是查询超时时间、M 是最大内存上限,两者都是运行时限流参数
M=每节点连边数(图稠密度)、ef_construction=建图候选广度;调大 recall 升,代价是更多内存/更长构建
M 控制向量维度、ef_construction 控制压缩比,和 recall 无关,只影响存储
两者都只影响查询延迟不影响 recall,调大只是让查询变慢没有质量收益
options_en: ef_construction is the query timeout and M is the memory cap; both are runtime throttling parameters.
M = links per node (graph density), ef_construction = build-time candidate breadth; raising them lifts recall at the cost of more memory / longer build.
M controls vector dimension and ef_construction controls compression ratio, unrelated to recall, affecting only storage.
Both only affect query latency, not recall; raising them just slows queries with no quality gain.
optionExplanations: 两者是建图参数不是运行时限流;混淆了 ef_construction 与查询期的 ef_search。
对;M 决定图多稠密(内存)、ef_construction 决定建图多仔细(构建时间),都换 recall。
M 和 ef_construction 都不改向量维度或压缩比,而是图结构质量参数。
它们确实影响 recall(建图质量决定检索质量),不是只影响延迟。
optionExplanations_en: Both are build parameters, not runtime throttles; this confuses ef_construction with query-time ef_search.
Correct — M sets graph density (memory) and ef_construction sets build thoroughness (build time), both trading for recall.
Neither M nor ef_construction changes vector dimension or compression; they are graph-quality parameters.
They do affect recall (build quality drives search quality), not just latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: HNSW 建图时每一步考察的候选邻居数,越大图质量越好、构建越慢。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ef_construction is how many candidate neighbors HNSW evaluates per build step; larger gives better graph quality but slower builds.

termDefinitions.meaning: HNSW 中每个节点保留的连接数,越大图越稠密、recall 越高、内存越多。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: M is the number of links kept per HNSW node; larger makes the graph denser with higher recall and more memory.

scenario: 十亿级 ANN 索引放不进单机内存,团队在「全内存分片」和「单机磁盘索引」之间选,系统有 p99<200ms 的硬约束。
scenario_en: A billion-scale ANN index won't fit one machine's RAM; the team weighs sharded in-memory vs single-node disk-based index, under a hard p99<200ms constraint.
q: 有严格 p99 约束时,in-memory 分片 vs 磁盘索引该怎么选?
q_en: With a strict p99 constraint, how do you choose in-memory sharding vs a disk-based index?
why: 磁盘索引更便宜但尾延迟高、容易顶破 p99;有严格 p99 时应把索引分片到多机内存并行查再合并,内存查询延迟低且稳定。代价是机器成本和分片/合并的运维复杂度。
why_en: Disk indexes are cheaper but have high tail latency that breaks p99, so under a strict p99 you shard the index across machines' RAM and query in parallel, paying with machine cost and shard-merge complexity.
tradeoff: 内存分片(低稳尾延迟,贵+运维复杂) vs 磁盘索引(便宜,尾延迟高易破 p99)
whenOtherWins: 如果没有严格实时 p99 要求(如离线批量检索或后台推荐预算),磁盘索引更省钱,尾延迟高一点可以接受。
options: 选磁盘索引:它尾延迟更低更稳定,内存索引反而 p99 波动大,成本还高
选内存分片:分片到多机内存并行查再合并,延迟低而稳,代价是机器成本+分片运维复杂度
两者随便选都行:p99 只由模型决定,索引存哪里不影响尾延迟
选单机全内存不分片:直接买一台超大内存机器,避免分片就没有合并开销和尾延迟
options_en: Pick disk: it has lower, steadier tail latency, while in-memory has high p99 jitter and costs more.
Pick in-memory sharding: shard across machines' RAM, query in parallel and merge for low steady latency, paying with machine cost and shard-merge ops complexity.
Either is fine: p99 is set by the model alone, and where the index lives does not affect tail latency.
Pick single-node all-in-memory without sharding: just buy one giant-RAM machine to avoid sharding, so there is no merge overhead or tail latency.
optionExplanations: 反了;磁盘索引尾延迟更高(冷读、寻道),恰恰是它容易破 p99,内存才低而稳。
对;严格 p99 下要低且稳定的延迟,内存分片并行查最合适,代价是钱和运维。
索引介质直接决定读取延迟,磁盘 vs 内存对尾延迟影响巨大,不能不管。
十亿索引装不进单机内存正是前提;硬扛超大内存机成本极高且有单点风险,分片才是常规解。
optionExplanations_en: Reversed — disk has higher tail latency (cold reads, seeks), which is exactly what breaks p99; RAM is the low, steady option.
Correct — a strict p99 needs low steady latency, so sharded in-memory parallel query fits best, paying with cost and ops.
The storage medium directly sets read latency; disk vs RAM hugely affects tail latency and cannot be ignored.
The premise is that a billion vectors do not fit one machine's RAM; forcing a giant-RAM box is very costly with single-point risk, so sharding is the norm.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把索引切成多份放到不同机器,查询并行发到所有分片再合并结果。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Sharding splits the index across machines, querying all shards in parallel and merging the results.

termDefinitions.meaning: 第 99 百分位延迟:99% 的请求快于这个值,衡量尾部体验。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: p99 is the 99th-percentile latency: 99% of requests are faster than this value, measuring tail experience.

scenario: 要为十亿向量选托管/自建向量库,团队小、想快速上线、能接受一定成本,但要求亚 10ms 检索且少运维。
scenario_en: Choosing a vector DB for a billion vectors: a small team wants fast time-to-market, accepts some cost, needs sub-10ms retrieval and minimal ops.
q: 小团队要少运维、快速上线,FAISS / ScaNN / Pinecone 该选哪个?
q_en: For a small team wanting minimal ops and fast launch, which of FAISS / ScaNN / Pinecone fits?
why: Pinecone 是托管 HNSW,亚 10ms 且免运维,最契合「小团队少运维快上线」。FAISS 最灵活但要自建自维;ScaNN 延迟最低但强绑 Google 基建。约束是运维成本而非极致延迟,所以选托管。
why_en: Pinecone is managed HNSW with sub-10ms latency and no ops, fitting a small team wanting a fast launch, while FAISS needs self-hosting and ScaNN couples to Google infra.
tradeoff: Pinecone(免运维,规模成本高+可调有限) vs FAISS(灵活最强,自建自维) vs ScaNN(延迟最低,绑 Google)
whenOtherWins: 如果要极致低延迟且已在 Google 基建上,ScaNN 亚 2ms(CPU)更优;如果要深度定制索引且有专人维护,FAISS 的灵活性无可替代。
options: 选 FAISS:它是托管服务免运维,小团队直接用最省心
选 ScaNN:它对小团队最友好、开箱即用且不依赖任何特定云
选 Pinecone:托管 HNSW、亚 10ms、免运维,契合小团队快上线,代价是规模成本与可调性有限
选自建 HNSW+PQ:虽然要养索引,但小团队更该从零手搓以获得完全控制
options_en: Pick FAISS: it is a managed no-ops service, easiest for a small team to just use.
Pick ScaNN: it is the most beginner-friendly, works out of the box, and depends on no particular cloud.
Pick Pinecone: managed HNSW, sub-10ms, no ops — fits a small team's fast launch, paying with scale cost and limited tunability.
Pick self-built HNSW+PQ: despite maintaining the index, a small team should hand-roll from scratch for full control.
optionExplanations: FAISS 是库不是托管服务,得自己部署运维,与「少运维」诉求相反。
ScaNN 延迟最低但强耦合 Google 基建,不是「不依赖特定云、开箱即用」。
对;托管+亚10ms+免运维正好命中小团队约束,代价是贵和调参空间小。
小团队最缺的就是维护索引的人力,从零手搓与「少运维快上线」正相反。
optionExplanations_en: FAISS is a library, not a managed service — you deploy and operate it yourself, contrary to the minimal-ops need.
ScaNN has the lowest latency but couples tightly to Google infra, so it is not cloud-agnostic or turnkey.
Correct — managed + sub-10ms + no ops hits the small-team constraint, paying with cost and limited tuning.
A small team most lacks the headcount to maintain an index, so hand-rolling contradicts minimal-ops fast-launch.

termDefinitions.meaning: Meta 开源的向量检索库,支持 IVF+PQ/HNSW,灵活但需自建自维。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: FAISS (Facebook AI Similarity Search) is Meta's open-source vector library supporting IVF+PQ/HNSW, flexible but self-hosted.

termDefinitions.meaning: Google 的向量检索库,用各向异性向量量化,CPU 上亚 2ms,但绑 Google 基建。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ScaNN (Scalable Nearest Neighbors) is Google's library using anisotropic quantization for sub-2ms CPU search, coupled to Google infra.

termDefinitions.meaning: 托管向量数据库,底层托管 HNSW,亚 10ms、免运维但规模成本较高。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pinecone is a managed vector database running managed HNSW with sub-10ms latency and no ops, at higher cost at scale.

scenario: 检索要按语言/地区/政策等元数据过滤,团队在 post-filtering 和 pre-filtering 之间权衡。
scenario_en: Retrieval must filter by metadata (language/region/policy), and the team weighs post-filtering vs pre-filtering.
q: post-filtering 和 pre-filtering 在机制和风险上有什么区别?
q_en: How do post-filtering and pre-filtering differ in mechanism and risk?
why: post-filtering:先 ANN 检索再丢掉不满足过滤的项——简单,但过滤太狠会让最终集合缩到不足 top-k,体验退化。pre-filtering:按元数据把索引分区、只搜相关分区——保证结果数量,但索引分区暴涨,存储与管理成本上升。
why_en: Post-filtering searches ANN first then drops items failing the filter (simple, but heavy filtering can shrink the set below top-k), while pre-filtering partitions the index by metadata and searches only the relevant partition (guarantees count but multiplies partitions).
tradeoff: post-filtering(简单,结果数可能不足 top-k) vs pre-filtering(保证数量,分区暴涨)
diagram:
flowchart TB
  subgraph Post[post-filtering]
    P1["ANN 检索 top-k"] --> P2["丢弃不合规项"] --> P3["可能少于 top-k"]
  end
  subgraph Pre[pre-filtering]
    R1["按元数据分区"] --> R2["只搜相关分区"] --> R3["保证结果数量"]
  end
options: post-filtering 先分区再搜、pre-filtering 先搜再丢,两者只是叫法不同结果一样
post-filtering 先 ANN 再丢不合规项(可能不足 top-k);pre-filtering 按元数据分区只搜相关区(保数量但分区暴涨)
两者都保证结果数量,区别只是 post 更快、pre 更省内存,没有其他取舍
post-filtering 只能过滤数值字段、pre-filtering 只能过滤文本字段,按字段类型二选一
options_en: Post-filtering partitions then searches, pre-filtering searches then drops — just different names for the same result.

Post-filtering runs ANN then drops non-compliant items (may fall below top-k); pre-filtering partitions the index by metadata and searches only the relevant partition (guarantees count but multiplies partitions).
Both guarantee result count, differing only in that post is faster and pre saves memory, with no other tradeoff.
Post-filtering can filter only numeric fields and pre-filtering only text fields, chosen by field type.
optionExplanations: 定义弄反了:post 是先搜后丢、pre 是先分区后搜,结果风险也不同。
对;核心区别是「先搜后丢会数量不足」vs「先分区保数量但分区膨胀」。
post 不保证数量(过滤后可能少于 top-k),这正是它的主要风险。
两者与字段是数值还是文本无关,过滤逻辑一样,区别在过滤发生在检索前还是后。
optionExplanations_en: Definitions reversed: post searches then drops, pre partitions then searches, with different risks.
Correct — the core difference is search-then-drop can under-fill vs partition-first guarantees count but bloats partitions.
Post does not guarantee count (may fall below top-k after filtering), which is its main risk.
Neither depends on numeric vs text fields; the filter logic is the same, differing in whether it runs before or after retrieval.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先做 ANN 检索,再把不满足元数据条件的结果丢掉。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Post-filtering runs ANN retrieval first, then drops results that fail the metadata condition.

termDefinitions.meaning: 先按元数据把索引分区,查询只在符合条件的分区里检索。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Pre-filtering partitions the index by metadata first, so a query only searches the qualifying partition.

scenario: 线上用 post-filtering,某些强过滤(小语种+特定地区)下,ANN 返回 top-k 后被过滤到只剩几条,结果集不足以填满页面。
scenario_en: In production with post-filtering, some strong filters (rare language + specific region) shrink the ANN top-k to just a few items, not enough to fill the page.
q: post-filtering 返回结果少于 top-k,最该怎么修?
q_en: When post-filtering returns fewer than top-k, what is the best fix?
why: 根因是「先检索再丢」在强过滤下会把集合丢到不足 top-k。最直接的修法是改成 pre-filtering:按该元数据把索引分区、只在相关分区里检索,从源头保证够 top-k 个合规候选。
why_en: The root cause is search-then-drop shrinking the set under strong filters, so the direct fix is pre-filtering: partition the index by that metadata and search only the relevant partition to guarantee enough compliant candidates.
tradeoff: pre-filtering(保证数量,分区管理成本) vs 继续 post-filtering(简单,强过滤下数量不足)
whenOtherWins: 如果过滤只是偶发轻度(大多数请求过滤后仍够 top-k),简单加大 over-retrieval 倍数继续 post-filtering 就够,不必上分区。
options: 调大 ANN 的 nprobe/ef 一直加,直到过滤后凑够 top-k,不改过滤策略
改成 pre-filtering:按该元数据把索引分区、只搜相关分区,从源头保证够 top-k 合规候选
放宽过滤条件、把不合规项也展示给用户,先保证数量再说
把 top-k 直接设成 1,只要有一条结果就不算「少于 top-k」
options_en: Keep raising ANN's nprobe/ef until enough survive filtering, without changing the filter strategy.
Switch to pre-filtering: partition the index by that metadata and search only the relevant partition, guaranteeing enough compliant candidates from the source.
Relax the filter and show non-compliant items to users, prioritizing count over compliance.
Set top-k to 1, so any single surviving result no longer counts as 'fewer than top-k'.
optionExplanations: 一味加大检索广度成本高且不稳,强过滤下仍可能不够,治标不治本。
对;分区检索让返回的每一条都天然合规,从根上保证数量,是标准解。
展示不合规项违反过滤本意(语言/地区/政策),是拿合规换数量,不可取。
把 top-k 降到 1 是掩盖问题,不能满足页面需要的结果数量。
optionExplanations_en: Just widening retrieval is costly and unstable, and may still under-fill under strong filters — treating the symptom.
Correct — partitioned search makes every returned item compliant by construction, guaranteeing count at the source, the standard fix.
Showing non-compliant items defeats the filter's purpose (language/region/policy), trading compliance for count.
Dropping top-k to 1 hides the problem and fails to deliver the result count the page needs.

termDefinitions.meaning: post-filtering 时多取几倍 top-k 候选,预留被过滤掉的余量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An over-retrieval multiplier fetches several times top-k in post-filtering to leave headroom for items that get filtered out.

scenario: 既有高基数维度(国家/语言,几百上千个值)又有低基数维度(是否成人内容等),想兼顾结果数量保证和分区可控。
scenario_en: You have both high-cardinality dims (country/language, hundreds of values) and low-cardinality dims (e.g. is-adult), and want both count guarantees and manageable partitions.
q: 同时有高基数和低基数过滤维度时,混合过滤该怎么分工?
q_en: With both high- and low-cardinality filter dims, how should hybrid filtering divide the work?
why: 对高基数维度(国家/语言)做 pre-filtering 分区,保证结果数量且分区数可控;对低基数维度用 post-filtering + over-retrieval 倍数在检索后过滤。这样既不让分区随所有维度组合爆炸,又保住数量。
why_en: Partition (pre-filter) on high-cardinality dims like country/language to guarantee count with a manageable partition count, and post-filter low-cardinality dims with an over-retrieval multiplier, so partitions don't explode across all dimension combinations.
tradeoff: 高基数 pre + 低基数 post(分区可控且保数量) vs 全维度 pre(分区组合爆炸)
whenOtherWins: 如果所有过滤维度都是低基数且过滤很轻,直接全 post-filtering + 适当过取倍数最简单,不必分区。
options: 对所有维度都做 pre-filtering 分区,维度越多分区越细,数量最有保证
对所有维度都做 post-filtering,统一在检索后过滤,避免任何分区管理
对高基数维度(国家/语言)pre 分区保数量,对低基数维度 post 过滤+过取倍数,避免分区爆炸
对低基数维度 pre 分区、高基数维度 post 过滤,因为低基数分区少最省事
options_en: Pre-filter (partition) on every dimension; the more dimensions the finer the partitions, best for count.
Post-filter every dimension, filtering uniformly after retrieval to avoid any partition management.
Pre-partition high-cardinality dims (country/language) to guarantee count, and post-filter low-cardinality dims with an over-retrieval multiplier, avoiding partition explosion.
Pre-partition low-cardinality dims and post-filter high-cardinality dims, since few low-cardinality partitions are simplest.
optionExplanations: 对所有维度分区会让分区数按维度组合指数爆炸,存储和管理不可控。
全 post 在强过滤维度上又会回到「数量不足 top-k」的老问题。
对;高基数维度分区数可控且保数量,低基数留给 post,兼顾两端,是混合过滤的标准分工。
反了:高基数才该分区(分区数由值域决定但仍可控且保数量),低基数分区收益小、更适合 post。
optionExplanations_en: Partitioning every dimension explodes partitions combinatorially, making storage and management unmanageable.
All-post reintroduces the under-top-k problem on strongly filtering dimensions.
Correct — high-cardinality partitions stay manageable and guarantee count, low-cardinality goes to post, balancing both, the standard hybrid split.
Reversed: high-cardinality dims are the ones to partition (guaranteeing count), while low-cardinality dims gain little from partitioning and suit post-filtering.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个维度可能取值的数量;国家/语言是高基数,布尔标记是低基数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cardinality is how many distinct values a dimension can take; country/language are high-cardinality, boolean flags are low.

scenario: 粗排要在 10-30ms 内给候选生成来的~1000 个候选打分,选出~100 个进精排。
scenario_en: Coarse ranking must score the ~1000 candidates from candidate generation in 10-30ms and pass ~100 to fine re-ranking.
q: 粗排(coarse ranking)用什么模型、吃什么特征、预算多少?
q_en: What models, features, and budget does coarse ranking use?
why: 粗排用轻量模型(逻辑回归/浅层 MLP/小 GBDT),吃 embedding 之外的特征(user-item 交互计数、时段、设备、简单交叉),预算 10-30ms,把~1000 筛到~100。它比候选生成用更多特征、但仍要快。
why_en: Coarse ranking uses light models (logistic regression, shallow MLP, small GBDT) with features beyond embeddings (interaction counts, time-of-day, device, simple crosses) in a 10-30ms budget, cutting ~1000 to ~100.
options: 用最重的 transformer 多任务模型,吃全部原始特征,预算放宽到 100ms 追求最高精度
只用两塔 embedding 的余弦相似度重排,不引入任何新特征,和候选生成完全一样
用轻量模型(LR/浅层 MLP/小 GBDT),吃交互计数/时段/设备等特征,预算 10-30ms,把~1000 筛到~100
不打分,直接按 item 热度排序取前 100,粗排本质是个热度榜
options_en: Use the heaviest multi-task transformer over all raw features, relaxing the budget to 100ms for max accuracy.
Just re-rank by two-tower embedding cosine similarity with no new features, identical to candidate generation.
Use light models (LR/shallow MLP/small GBDT) over interaction counts/time-of-day/device features in a 10-30ms budget, cutting ~1000 to ~100.
Do not score at all; sort by item popularity and take the top 100 — coarse ranking is essentially a popularity board.
optionExplanations: 重 transformer + 100ms 是精排的做法,粗排要在千级候选上保持轻快。
粗排的价值正是引入 embedding 之外的新特征,只用余弦相似度等于没做粗排。
对;轻模型 + 交互/上下文特征 + 10-30ms,是粗排的标准配置。
纯热度榜忽略了个性化交互特征,粗排要打个性化分而非全局热度。
optionExplanations_en: Heavy transformer + 100ms is fine-ranking; coarse ranking must stay light over thousands of candidates.
Coarse ranking's value is adding features beyond embeddings; cosine-only means no real coarse ranking.
Correct — light models + interaction/context features + 10-30ms is the standard coarse-ranking setup.
A pure popularity board ignores personalized interaction features; coarse ranking scores personalization, not global popularity.

termDefinitions.meaning: 梯度提升树,轻量高效的表格特征打分模型,常用于粗排。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: GBDT (Gradient Boosted Decision Trees) is a light, efficient tabular scoring model often used for coarse ranking.

termDefinitions.meaning: 多层感知机,基础的全连接前馈神经网络。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: MLP (Multi-Layer Perceptron) is a basic fully-connected feedforward neural network.

scenario: 粗排 p99 超预算。工程师第一反应是换更快的模型,但 profiling 显示模型推理只占一小部分。
scenario_en: Coarse ranking's p99 is over budget. The instinct is a faster model, but profiling shows inference is only a small fraction.
q: 粗排延迟的主要瓶颈通常是什么?该往哪里优化?
q_en: What is coarse ranking's dominant latency bottleneck, and where should you optimize?
why: 粗排要给~1000 个候选各取几百个特征,主要时间花在 feature store 检索而非模型推理。优化点是特征取用的批量化/缓存(一次批量取、缓存热特征),而不是换更快的模型。
why_en: Coarse ranking fetches hundreds of features for each of ~1000 candidates, so feature-store retrieval — not model inference — dominates latency, and the fix is batching/caching feature lookups.
tradeoff: 优化特征取用(批量+缓存,治本) vs 换更快模型(推理本就不是瓶颈,收效甚微)
whenOtherWins: 如果 profiling 显示推理确实占大头(如误用了重模型做粗排),那才该先换轻模型或量化;瓶颈定位要以实测为准。
diagram:
flowchart LR C["~1000 候选"] --> F["feature store 批量取
数百特征×1000 (主瓶颈)"] F --> M["轻量模型推理
(占比小)"] M --> O["~100 候选"]
options: 瓶颈是模型推理,应把模型换成更小的或量化,feature store 取用可忽略
瓶颈是 feature store 检索(数百特征×1000 候选),应做批量取用+缓存热特征,而非只换模型
瓶颈是网络带宽,应把粗排服务和候选生成部署到同一进程消除 RPC
瓶颈是 GPU 显存不足,应加显存把 batch 开大,与特征取用无关
options_en: The bottleneck is model inference; swap in a smaller or quantized model — feature-store lookups are negligible.
The bottleneck is feature-store retrieval (hundreds of features × 1000 candidates); batch the lookups and cache hot features rather than just swapping models.
The bottleneck is network bandwidth; co-locate coarse ranking and candidate generation in one process to eliminate RPC.
The bottleneck is GPU memory; add VRAM to enlarge the batch, unrelated to feature lookups.
optionExplanations: profiling 明确显示推理只占一小部分,换模型救不了主要延迟。
对;数百特征×1000 候选的取用才是大头,批量化+缓存才治本。
带宽不是这里的主因;主要是特征取用的次数与延迟,批量取才是关键。
粗排轻模型显存压力小,瓶颈在取特征而非显存或 batch 大小。
optionExplanations_en: Profiling clearly shows inference is a small fraction, so swapping models won't fix the main latency.
Correct — hundreds of features × 1000 candidates dominates; batching plus caching is the real fix.
Bandwidth is not the main cause here; it's the count and latency of feature lookups, so batching them is key.
A light coarse model has little VRAM pressure; the bottleneck is feature fetching, not memory or batch size.

termDefinitions.meaning: 在线存取模型特征的低延迟服务,推理前批量取候选的特征。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A feature store is a low-latency service for serving model features, batch-fetched for candidates before inference.

scenario: 精排只需处理~100 个候选,预算可放宽到 20-50ms,要用最有表达力的模型。
scenario_en: Fine re-ranking handles only ~100 candidates with a relaxed 20-50ms budget and uses the most expressive models.
q: 精排为什么用得起最重的模型?典型用哪些模型、叠加什么?
q_en: Why can fine re-ranking afford the heaviest models, and what models/overlays does it use?
why: 候选已被前两级砍到~100,小集合让重模型的高单价可承受,预算放宽到 20-50ms。典型模型:Deep Cross Network、多任务(联合建 engagement+satisfaction)、建模 item 间依赖的 transformer;之后叠加多样性/新鲜度/政策等业务规则。
why_en: With only ~100 candidates left, the small set justifies expensive models in a 20-50ms budget, using DCN, multi-task models (engagement+satisfaction), and inter-item transformers, then business overlays like diversity/freshness/policy.
options: 因为精排在 CPU 上跑没有 GPU 成本,所以可以任意加大模型
候选已砍到~100,小集合让重模型可承受(20-50ms);用 DCN/多任务/inter-item transformer,再叠多样性/新鲜度/政策
因为精排结果会被缓存复用,单次算多贵都摊薄了,所以模型无上限
因为精排不需要取特征,省下的时间全给模型,所以能上超大模型
options_en: Because fine ranking runs on CPU with no GPU cost, so the model can grow arbitrarily.
Candidates are already cut to ~100, so the small set justifies heavy models (20-50ms); use DCN/multi-task/inter-item transformers, then overlay diversity/freshness/policy.
Because fine-ranking results are cached and reused, amortizing any per-call cost, so the model is unbounded.
Because fine ranking needs no feature fetching, all saved time goes to the model, enabling a huge model.
optionExplanations: 精排多在 GPU 上跑重模型,不是靠 CPU 免成本;根因是候选少了单价可承受。
对;小集合摊得起高单价,才用 DCN/多任务/transformer 并叠业务规则。
精排结果高度个性化+时效,难长期缓存复用;能上重模型是因候选少。
精排照样要取特征;能上重模型的根因是候选数从千级降到百级。
optionExplanations_en: Fine ranking usually runs heavy models on GPU, not free CPU; the reason is fewer candidates make per-item cost affordable.
Correct — a small set affords high per-item cost, enabling DCN/multi-task/transformers plus business overlays.
Fine-ranking results are highly personalized and time-sensitive, hard to cache long-term; heavy models are afforded by few candidates.
Fine ranking still fetches features; the reason heavy models are affordable is candidates dropping from thousands to hundreds.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个模型同时预测多个目标(如点击 engagement 与满意度 satisfaction),共享表示。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A multi-task model jointly predicts several targets (e.g. engagement and satisfaction) with a shared representation.

termDefinitions.term: business-logic overlay / 业务规则叠加
termDefinitions.meaning: 在模型分之上叠加的硬规则:多样性、新鲜度提升、政策过滤等。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Business-logic overlays are hard rules applied on top of model scores: diversity, freshness boosting, policy filters.

scenario: 精排纯按分数排,结果前 5 个视频全来自同一个创作者,用户体验单调。
scenario_en: Ranking purely by score, the top 5 videos all come from one creator, making the feed monotonous.
q: 为什么精排后要加多样性等业务规则?不加会怎样?
q_en: Why add diversity and other business rules after fine ranking, and what happens without them?
why: 纯分数最优会让高分来源(同一创作者/同一话题)扎堆,体验单调、长期伤留存。多样性约束(限制同源占比)、新鲜度提升、政策过滤是叠在模型分之上的硬规则,把「单次相关最优」修正成「整体体验最优」。代价是牺牲一点单点相关性。
why_en: Pure top-score ranking clusters items from one source, hurting experience and retention, so diversity/freshness/policy overlays trade a bit of per-item relevance for better overall experience.
tradeoff: 多样性规则(整体体验更好,牺牲单点相关) vs 纯分数(单点最优但扎堆单调)
options: 不用加;模型分已经是最优,任何业务规则都只会降低质量
加规则是为了合规审计留痕,与用户体验无关,不加也不影响观感
纯分数会让同源/同话题扎堆、体验单调伤留存;多样性/新鲜度/政策规则把单点最优修正成整体最优,代价是牺牲一点相关性
加规则是为了降低精排延迟,规则能提前砍掉候选让模型少算
options_en: No need; the model score is already optimal and any business rule only lowers quality.
Rules exist for compliance audit trails, unrelated to user experience, and skipping them doesn't affect the feel.

Pure scoring clusters same-source/same-topic items, making the feed monotonous and hurting retention; diversity/freshness/policy overlays fix per-item-optimal into overall-optimal at the cost of some relevance.
Rules exist to cut fine-ranking latency by pruning candidates so the model computes less.
optionExplanations: 模型分优化的是单点相关,不含整体多样性;不加规则会扎堆,并非任何规则都降质。
多样性/新鲜度直接改变用户看到的排列,是体验问题不是纯审计。
对;规则把「单条最相关」修正为「整页最好看」,代价是略降单点相关性。
业务规则是排序后叠加的重排,不是为降延迟砍候选。
optionExplanations_en: The model score optimizes per-item relevance, not overall diversity; without rules items cluster, and not every rule lowers quality.
Diversity/freshness directly change what the user sees — an experience issue, not mere auditing.
Correct — rules turn most-relevant-per-item into best-overall-page, at the cost of slightly lower per-item relevance.
Business rules are a post-ranking rerank, not candidate pruning to cut latency.

termDefinitions.meaning: 限制结果里同一来源/话题的占比,避免扎堆,提升整体体验。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A diversity constraint caps how many results share one source/topic to avoid clustering and improve overall experience.

scenario: 精排想上更大的 transformer 提升相关性,但单次推理逼近 50ms 预算上限,不能简单换回小模型。
scenario_en: Fine ranking wants a bigger transformer for relevance but inference nears the 50ms budget cap, and reverting to a small model isn't acceptable.
q: 精排面临「相关性 vs 延迟」矛盾时,怎么在不明显掉精度下压延迟?
q_en: Facing the relevance-vs-latency conflict in fine ranking, how do you cut latency without visibly losing accuracy?
why: 用量化(降精度加速)+知识蒸馏(把大模型能力压进小学生模型)在几乎不掉精度的前提下降延迟。相比直接换回小模型丢相关性、或硬扛大模型超预算,这是保住相关性又满足延迟的中间路。
why_en: Use quantization (lower precision for speed) plus knowledge distillation (compress the big model into a smaller student) to cut latency with minimal accuracy loss, unlike simply reverting to a small model.
tradeoff: 量化+蒸馏(几乎不掉精度地降延迟,需额外工程) vs 换小模型(简单但丢相关性)
whenOtherWins: 如果相关性差一点无所谓、工程资源紧张,直接用现成小模型最省事;蒸馏/量化的额外训练与验证成本只有在相关性关键时才值得。
options: 直接把 transformer 换成逻辑回归,虽然掉相关性但一定不超时,简单可靠
用量化(降精度加速)+知识蒸馏(大模型能力压进小模型),几乎不掉精度地压延迟
把精排预算从 50ms 硬调到 200ms,不改模型,让它慢慢算完
对每个请求缓存精排结果,第二次直接返回,绕开延迟问题
options_en: Just replace the transformer with logistic regression: it loses relevance but never times out — simple and reliable.
Use quantization (lower precision for speed) plus knowledge distillation (compress the big model into a small student) to cut latency with almost no accuracy loss.
Hard-raise the fine-ranking budget from 50ms to 200ms without changing the model, letting it finish slowly.
Cache each request's fine-ranking result and return it on the second hit, sidestepping the latency problem.
optionExplanations: 换 LR 是拿相关性换延迟,与「不明显掉精度」的目标冲突。
对;量化+蒸馏在保住相关性的同时降延迟,是相关性关键时的标准解。
把 p99 预算从 50ms 抬到 200ms 违反 SLA,是放弃延迟目标不是解决矛盾。
精排结果高度个性化时效强,难缓存复用,治标不治本。
optionExplanations_en: Swapping to LR trades relevance for latency, conflicting with the no-visible-accuracy-loss goal.
Correct — quantization plus distillation cut latency while preserving relevance, the standard fix when relevance matters.
Raising the p99 budget from 50ms to 200ms violates the SLA — abandoning the latency goal, not resolving the conflict.
Highly personalized, time-sensitive fine-ranking results are hard to cache, so this treats the symptom.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用大模型(teacher)的输出训练小模型(student),把能力压进更快的小模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Knowledge distillation trains a small student model on a big teacher's outputs, compressing capability into a faster model.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把权重/激活从高精度(FP32)降到低精度(FP16/INT8),加速推理、省内存。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Quantization lowers weights/activations from high precision (FP32) to low (FP16/INT8), speeding inference and saving memory.

q: 填空:三级漏斗每级的候选量级与延迟预算。
q_en: Fill in each funnel stage's candidate scale and latency budget.
text_en: Candidate generation: billions → ~{{500-2000}} candidates, budget {{10-20}}ms; coarse ranking: ~1000 → ~{{100}}, budget {{10-30}}ms; fine re-ranking: ~100 → final, budget {{20-50}}ms.
why: 记住量级递减(十亿→千→百)与预算递增(候选越少、模型越重、越舍得给时间)的对应关系:总预算被三级瓜分,任何一级超支都会顶破 p99。
why_en: Remember the shrinking counts (billions→thousands→hundreds) paired with growing budgets, since the total p99 is split across the three stages.

termDefinitions.meaning: 分配给某一级的时间上限,各级之和不能超过端到端 p99 目标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A latency budget is the time ceiling allotted to a stage; the stages must sum within the end-to-end p99 target.

q: 填空:三级漏斗每一级在做的核心权衡。
q_en: Fill in the core tradeoff each funnel stage makes.
text: 漏斗每一级都用「更{{少}}的候选」换「更{{强}}的模型」——即拿{{广度}}换{{深度}};候选生成盯 {{recall}}(漏了不可恢复),后两级盯精度。
text_en: Each funnel stage trades {{fewer}} candidates for a {{heavier}} model — i.e. {{breadth}} for {{depth}}; candidate generation optimizes {{recall}} (misses are unrecoverable), later stages optimize precision.
why: 一句话记住漏斗:广度换深度。第一级 recall 优先(漏项不可逆),越往后候选越少、模型越重、越追求精度。
why_en: One-liner for the funnel: trade breadth for depth, with recall first up front (misses are irreversible) and precision growing downstream.

termDefinitions.meaning: 返回结果中真正相关的比例;后两级排序追求把最相关的排到最前。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Precision is the fraction of returned results that are truly relevant; later ranking stages push the most relevant to the top.

scenario: 要给候选生成阶段定一个主指标来指导迭代;有人提议用 precision@k,有人提议 recall@k。
scenario_en: You must pick a primary metric to guide candidate-generation iteration; some propose precision@k, others recall@k.
q: 候选生成该以 recall@k 还是 precision@k 为主指标?为什么?
q_en: Should candidate generation optimize recall@k or precision@k, and why?
why: 候选生成盯 recall@k:它的职责是「别漏掉相关项」,漏了下游永远补不回来;精度(把最相关排最前)是后两级排序的活。用 precision 当主指标会奖励「少而准」,反而放大漏召回风险。
why_en: Candidate generation optimizes recall@k because its job is to not miss relevant items (misses are unrecoverable downstream), while precision — putting the most relevant on top — is the later ranking stages' job.
tradeoff: recall@k(不漏相关项,可能带进噪声由下游筛) vs precision@k(准但易漏,漏了不可逆)
whenOtherWins: 如果下游排序能力很弱、无法从噪声候选里挑出好结果,那才需要候选生成本身更看重 precision;通常下游足够强,recall 优先。
options: 以 precision@k 为主:候选越准下游越省事,漏一点相关项无所谓
以 recall@k 为主:职责是不漏相关项(漏了下游补不回),精度交给后两级排序
两个都不用,直接用点击率 CTR 当候选生成的主指标最贴近业务
用延迟当唯一主指标:候选生成只要够快,召回精度都不重要
options_en: Optimize precision@k: more precise candidates ease downstream, and missing a few relevant items is fine.
Optimize recall@k: the job is not to miss relevant items (misses are unrecoverable downstream), leaving precision to later ranking stages.
Use neither; use click-through rate (CTR) as the primary metric since it is closest to business.
Use latency as the sole primary metric: as long as candidate generation is fast, recall and precision don't matter.
optionExplanations: 漏召回不可逆,precision 优先会奖励「少而漏」,与候选生成的职责相悖。
对;候选生成的天条是别漏相关项,精度是下游排序的目标。
CTR 是端到端业务指标,受下游排序主导,无法单独指导候选生成的召回。
只看延迟会牺牲召回质量;快但漏一堆相关项没有意义。
optionExplanations_en: Misses are irreversible; prioritizing precision rewards few-but-missing, contradicting candidate generation's job.
Correct — candidate generation's cardinal rule is not to miss relevant items, leaving precision to downstream ranking.
CTR is an end-to-end business metric dominated by downstream ranking and cannot alone guide candidate-generation recall.
Optimizing latency alone sacrifices recall; fast but missing many relevant items is pointless.

termDefinitions.meaning: 返回前 k 个里相关项的比例;衡量「准不准」,是排序阶段目标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Precision@k is the fraction of the top-k that are relevant, measuring accuracy — the ranking stages' goal.

termDefinitions.meaning: 点击率:展示中被点击的比例,端到端业务指标。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CTR (Click-Through Rate) is the fraction of impressions that get clicked, an end-to-end business metric.

scenario: 十亿级 ANN 索引已分片到多机,单个分片机器偶发宕机会让该分片的候选全查不到,且流量峰值时单副本扛不住。
scenario_en: A billion-scale ANN index is sharded across machines; a shard node's occasional crash makes that shard's candidates unreachable, and one replica can't absorb peak traffic.
q: 十亿级索引除了分片,为什么还要副本(replication)?
q_en: Beyond sharding, why does a billion-scale index also need replication?
why: 分片解决「装不下+并行查」,但单分片宕机会丢该分片全部候选、且单副本扛不住峰值。副本给每个分片多份拷贝→容错(挂一份还有别份)+负载均衡(峰值分摊到多副本)。代价是存储与同步成本翻倍。
why_en: Sharding solves capacity and parallelism, but replication adds copies per shard for fault tolerance (survive a node loss) and load balancing (spread peak traffic), at the cost of extra storage and sync.
options: 副本是为了提高召回率:多份索引投票取交集能提升 recall,与容错无关
副本给每个分片多份拷贝→容错(挂一份还有别份)+负载均衡(峰值分摊),代价是存储/同步翻倍
副本是为了压缩内存:每份副本存不同精度,合起来省显存
有了分片就不需要副本,分片已经天然容错,加副本纯属浪费
options_en: Replication boosts recall: multiple index copies vote and intersect to raise recall, unrelated to fault tolerance.
Replication adds copies per shard for fault tolerance (survive one node's loss) and load balancing (spread peak traffic), at the cost of doubled storage/sync.
Replication compresses memory: each replica stores a different precision, together saving VRAM.
Sharding removes the need for replication — shards are inherently fault-tolerant, so replicas are pure waste.
optionExplanations: 副本存的是同一份数据的拷贝,不是投票机制,和 recall 提升无关。
对;分片管容量与并行,副本管容错与负载,是两个正交维度。
副本是相同数据的冗余拷贝,不是不同精度分层,压缩是 PQ 的活。
分片本身没有冗余,单分片宕机就丢该分片数据,必须靠副本容错。
optionExplanations_en: Replicas are copies of the same data, not a voting scheme, and don't raise recall.
Correct — sharding handles capacity/parallelism while replication handles fault tolerance/load, two orthogonal axes.
Replicas are redundant copies of identical data, not mixed-precision tiers; compression is PQ's job.
Sharding alone has no redundancy — one shard's crash loses that shard's data, so replication is required for fault tolerance.

termDefinitions.meaning: 为每个分片保存多份相同拷贝,用于容错和分摊查询负载。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Replication keeps multiple identical copies of each shard for fault tolerance and to spread query load.

scenario: 检索既要向量语义相似,又要能按关键词命中和复杂元数据过滤(如同时匹配品牌词并限定地区),团队想少运维。
scenario_en: Retrieval needs vector semantic similarity plus keyword hits and complex metadata filters (e.g. match a brand term and restrict region), with minimal ops.
q: 需要「向量+关键词混合检索且带复杂元数据过滤」时,四个候选里 Weaviate 相对更合适在哪?
q_en: When you need hybrid vector+keyword retrieval with complex metadata filters, why is Weaviate relatively fitting among the four?
why: Weaviate 原生支持 HNSW + 关键词的混合检索和元数据过滤,契合「语义+关键词+复杂过滤」需求。代价是复杂过滤下延迟会上升;若只需纯向量亚 10ms,Pinecone/FAISS/ScaNN 更简单快。
why_en: Weaviate natively supports HNSW plus keyword hybrid search and metadata filtering, fitting semantic+keyword+complex-filter needs, at the cost of higher latency under complex filters.
tradeoff: Weaviate(混合检索+元数据过滤灵活,复杂过滤延迟高) vs 纯向量库(更快但过滤/关键词弱)
whenOtherWins: 如果只需纯向量相似度、不要关键词或复杂过滤且要极致低延迟,ScaNN/Pinecone 更快更简单,不需要 Weaviate 的混合能力。
options: Weaviate 延迟最低,任何复杂过滤下都比其他三个快,所以选它
Weaviate 原生支持 HNSW+关键词混合检索和元数据过滤,契合语义+关键词+复杂过滤,代价是复杂过滤延迟升高
Weaviate 是唯一支持 GPU 的向量库,靠 GPU 算力做混合检索
Weaviate 压缩率最高,靠 PQ 把索引压到最小,所以适合复杂过滤
options_en: Weaviate has the lowest latency and beats the other three under any complex filter, so pick it.
Weaviate natively supports HNSW + keyword hybrid search and metadata filtering, fitting semantic+keyword+complex filters, at the cost of higher latency under complex filters.
Weaviate is the only GPU-capable vector DB and does hybrid search via GPU compute.
Weaviate has the highest compression, using PQ to shrink the index, which suits complex filtering.
optionExplanations: Weaviate 在复杂过滤下延迟反而升高,并非最低延迟;它胜在混合检索能力。
对;它的差异化是混合检索+灵活元数据过滤,而不是极致延迟。
GPU 支持不是 Weaviate 的卖点(FAISS 也有 GPU);它的卖点是混合检索。
压缩率不是 Weaviate 的差异点;它靠原生混合检索+过滤取胜。
optionExplanations_en: Weaviate's latency actually rises under complex filters, so it is not the lowest; its edge is hybrid search.
Correct — its differentiator is hybrid retrieval plus flexible metadata filtering, not peak latency.
GPU support is not Weaviate's selling point (FAISS also has GPU); its selling point is hybrid search.
Compression is not Weaviate's differentiator; it wins on native hybrid search plus filtering.

termDefinitions.meaning: 支持 HNSW + 关键词混合检索与元数据过滤的向量数据库。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Weaviate is a vector database supporting HNSW plus keyword hybrid search and metadata filtering.

termDefinitions.meaning: 同时用向量语义相似度和关键词/词法匹配打分,再融合排序。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hybrid search scores by both vector semantic similarity and keyword/lexical match, then fuses the rankings.

scenario: 面试官追问:候选生成用 ANN,那 ANN 的 recall 和延迟能同时拉满吗?
scenario_en: The interviewer probes: with ANN in candidate generation, can you max out both recall and latency at once?
q: ANN 检索里 recall 和延迟是什么关系?这对参数调优意味着什么?
q_en: What is the relationship between recall and latency in ANN search, and what does it mean for tuning?
why: ANN 是近似检索:搜得越广(HNSW 的 ef_search、IVF 的 nprobe 越大)recall 越高但延迟越高,二者是此消彼长。调优就是在 p99 预算内把 recall 顶到最高,而非同时拉满——鱼与熊掌不可兼得。
why_en: ANN is approximate: searching wider (higher ef_search/nprobe) raises recall but also latency, so tuning maximizes recall within the p99 budget rather than maxing both.
tradeoff: 搜索更广(recall 高、延迟高) vs 搜索更窄(延迟低、recall 低)
options: recall 和延迟无关,可以同时拉满,只要机器够快
recall 越高延迟一定越低,二者正相关,调大搜索广度双赢
搜得越广 recall 越高但延迟也越高,二者此消彼长;调优是在 p99 预算内把 recall 顶到最高
延迟只由向量维度决定,与搜索广度无关,调 ef_search/nprobe 不影响延迟
options_en: Recall and latency are unrelated and can both be maxed, given fast enough machines.
Higher recall always means lower latency — they are positively correlated, so widening the search is win-win.
Searching wider raises recall but also latency — they trade off; tuning maximizes recall within the p99 budget.
Latency depends only on vector dimension, unrelated to search breadth, so ef_search/nprobe don't affect latency.
optionExplanations: 近似检索里 recall 与延迟由搜索广度耦合,加机器改变不了单查询的此消彼长。
方向反了:recall 高通常伴随延迟高,不是延迟低。
对;这就是 ANN 调优的本质——在延迟预算内尽量拉高 recall。
ef_search/nprobe 直接决定扫描量,是延迟主因,不能说与广度无关。
optionExplanations_en: In approximate search recall and latency are coupled by search breadth; adding machines doesn't remove the per-query tradeoff.
Direction reversed: high recall usually comes with high latency, not low.
Correct — this is the essence of ANN tuning: push recall as high as possible within the latency budget.
ef_search/nprobe directly set scan volume and are the main latency driver, so they're not unrelated to breadth.

termDefinitions.meaning: HNSW 查询期考察的候选数,越大 recall 越高、延迟越高(与建图期 ef_construction 不同)。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ef_search is HNSW's query-time candidate breadth; larger raises recall and latency (distinct from build-time ef_construction).

scenario: 有人提议砍掉粗排,让候选生成的~1000 候选直接进精排,以简化流水线。
scenario_en: Someone proposes dropping coarse ranking and feeding candidate generation's ~1000 candidates straight into fine re-ranking to simplify the pipeline.
q: 如果砍掉粗排,直接让~1000 候选进精排,会发生什么?
q_en: What happens if you skip coarse ranking and feed ~1000 candidates directly into fine re-ranking?
why: 精排是最贵的模型,只在~100 候选上跑才付得起。让~1000 直接进精排会让精排算力/延迟约 10× 膨胀,顶破 20-50ms 预算。粗排的作用正是用轻量模型把千级先削到百级,为精排减负。
why_en: Fine ranking is the most expensive model and only affordable on ~100 candidates, so feeding ~1000 inflates its compute/latency roughly 10x and blows the budget — coarse ranking exists to pre-cut thousands to hundreds.
options: 没影响:精排本来就能处理任意数量候选,砍掉粗排能简化系统还更准
精排延迟大降:候选虽多但精排会自动只挑前 100 个算,其余跳过
精排算力/延迟约 10× 膨胀顶破预算;粗排的作用正是用轻模型把千级削到百级为精排减负
候选生成会补偿:检测到没有粗排后自动把候选压到 100,无需精排改动
options_en: No impact: fine ranking can handle any candidate count, so dropping coarse ranking simplifies and improves accuracy.
Fine-ranking latency drops sharply: despite more candidates, it auto-picks only the top 100 to score and skips the rest.
Fine-ranking compute/latency inflates ~10x and blows the budget; coarse ranking exists to pre-cut thousands to hundreds and unload fine ranking.
Candidate generation compensates: detecting no coarse stage, it auto-compresses candidates to 100 with no fine-ranking change.
optionExplanations: 精排单价高,候选从 100 涨到 1000 直接约 10× 成本,不可能又快又准。
精排不会「自动只算前 100」——判断谁是前 100 正是粗排要先做的事。
对;粗排是精排的减负阀门,砍掉它精排就被千级候选压垮。
候选生成不感知下游是否有粗排,也不负责把候选压到百级,那是粗排的职责。
optionExplanations_en: Fine ranking is costly per item, so going from 100 to 1000 candidates ~10x's cost — it cannot stay fast and accurate.
Fine ranking cannot auto-score only the top 100 — deciding which 100 is exactly coarse ranking's job.
Correct — coarse ranking is the relief valve for fine ranking; drop it and fine ranking is crushed by thousands.
Candidate generation is unaware of downstream stages and doesn't compress to hundreds — that is coarse ranking's role.

termDefinitions.meaning: 漏斗第二级:轻量模型给千级候选打分,削到百级交给精排。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Coarse ranking is the funnel's second stage: a light model scores thousands of candidates down to hundreds for fine re-ranking.
